stages.title: The Theory
body: Hospitality businesses and job roles
Which jobs help a hospitality business work?
Point, say, draw or write.
stages.notes: Untimed opening. Read the question and explain that learners will choose a role for the next blog and CV lessons. The title “The Theory” is the workbook session label; keep the descriptive subtitle. Source: sources/MTP.xlsx; revision sha256:0895674f2901b602daf998b8a7aa1516522ce0c301b23bfba941fcc1807977cd. Medium Term Plan!C6; Lesson register!F6.

stages.title: Arrival task
body: Which challenges are on your Plan?
What does hospitality mean?
A knife is left on the counter. What do you do?
Does a hotel only employ receptionists?
BLUE / GREEN / AMBER / RED. Pause, breathe or choose a quieter seat.
stages.notes: 4 minutes. Regulation: BLUE low energy; GREEN ready; AMBER tense; RED overwhelmed. Offer water, quiet breathing, a brief pause or a quieter seat. Do not require a public colour disclosure. Privately agree the first return action and keep access to the task. Accept pointing or a short spoken answer. Expected answers: check the learner’s own agreed Plan; looking after guests/customers; leave the knife alone, keep clear and tell the adult; no, hotels also employ housekeepers, chefs and porters. No handling task is required. If the earlier Plan is unavailable, give the retrieval question as a private check and record the gap; do not pretend it was agreed. No cold calling or pair work. Use individual stations and a private check-in. Read, rephrase or scribe the learner’s own words; record support. Do not supply the learner’s assessed choice or explanation. Offer a quiet reset, then one clear return step. Only VF, WS, I, NS, E and R are used; confirm local code definitions before marking. E does not establish an award claim.

stages.title: Hospitality or another service
body: Café · bus · hotel · hospital · pub · festival bar
Which examples provide food, drink or a place to stay for guests?
I chose __ because __.
stages.notes: 2 minutes. Sort with an adult at the board; learners can point or say their choice. For this introductory sort, café, hotel, pub and festival bar are the hospitality examples. A bus is transport. A hospital’s main purpose is health care, although it also has catering and cleaning work. Explain this boundary rather than marking all work in a hospital as non-hospitality. No actual visit, alcohol handling or sale is involved.

stages.title: Today I can
body: Name five types of hospitality business and match job roles to them.
I can match a role to a business.
I can say what the person does.
I can choose a role that interests me.
stages.notes: Untimed. Read the exact workbook outcome. [QUAL] — planner mapping. The learner-friendly criteria unpack the activity and do not quote official assessment criteria. Exact official wording remains [VERIFY] until checked against the supplied official student book.

stages.title: Hotel jobs
body: Receptionist: welcomes guests and checks bookings.
Housekeeper: cleans and prepares rooms.
Chef: prepares food.
Porter: helps move guests’ luggage.
A __ works in a hotel and __.
stages.notes: 5 minutes. Draw or display one editable Hotel branch and add the four role labels as the model. Read one task at a time. Ask a private hinge: “Would the hotel work with a receptionist but nobody preparing rooms?” Expected no; a clean, ready room needs housekeeping. The model shows that businesses need several roles. The task statements are simple classroom examples, not universal job descriptions.

stages.title: Our shared mind map
body: Choose one business type and one job role.
Put your name or learner code on your sticky note.
Add your own words to the class mind map.
My business is __. The role is __.
stages.notes: 5 minutes. Each learner contributes independently from a station; the adult places notes on the shared sheet if needed. Scribe only the learner’s words and mark that support. Record who contributed what and the handover into the class product. Do not allocate a ready-made answer as the learner’s contribution. Hinge: a photo shows the whole map but no identifiable notes. Is individual ownership clear? Expected no; identify the learner’s own note before capture. No cold calling.

stages.title: Your Business and Jobs record
body: Record five business types.
For each business, give two job roles and one task for each role.
Then circle the role that interests you most.
A __ works at a __ and __.
Supported: Match cards and dictate a task for each role.
Independent: Complete five businesses and ten roles with tasks.
Aspire: Add an overlooked role and explain its value.
stages.notes: 12 minutes. This is the first part of the 18-minute individual task. Provide the blank ten-row evidence record. Read-only role cards support matching. An MCQ match is a recorded learner choice, not an adult answer. Check two rows early and correct misconceptions through a question. Some roles can belong to more than one business; accept a sensible task and explanation.

route_tasks.Supported: Match business and role cards. Say or dictate one task for each role.
route_tasks.Independent: Complete five businesses and ten roles with tasks. Choose your preferred role.
route_tasks.Aspire: Add an overlooked role and explain why the business needs it.

stages.title: Your evidence
body: Mark your own sticky note in the mind-map photo.
Check your five businesses and ten roles.
Complete: I chose __ because __.
Keep the photo reference and your own record together.
Supported: Find your note. Check with an adult reader.
Independent: Label both items and check the role tasks.
Aspire: Explain your preferred role using a reason.
stages.notes: 6 minutes. This completes the workbook’s 18-minute You Do. VOC1-L1-E1 is the identifiable contribution photo; VOC1-L1-E2 is the individual Business and Jobs record. Use approved adult equipment for the photo; learners need no phones. Keep the actual photo reference blank until captured. Record support separately and retain the learner’s own words.

route_tasks.Supported: Point to your own note. Use the checklist with an adult reader.
route_tasks.Independent: Label both evidence items and check every task matches its role.
route_tasks.Aspire: Explain why your chosen role suits your interests, using a reason.

stages.title: Tidy and check
body: Put your record and photo reference in your folder.
Check: five businesses, two jobs each, one task per job.
Is your own contribution easy to find?
I still need to __.
stages.notes: 4 minutes. Tidy the station and file the individual record. Store the photo/reference in the evidence app using the approved workflow. The photo alone is insufficient without ownership. Record actual duration, contribution and support; leave actual minutes and date blank until taught. Hospitality minutes are separate from Careers. Do not automatically claim the challenge completed.

stages.title: Exit ticket
body: Name your chosen job role.
Say one thing that person does.
My chosen role is __. One task is __.
stages.notes: 2 minutes. Private adult check, pointing or a short written answer. Expected example: receptionist, checks bookings. Accept any sensible chosen role/task pair. Use the answer to select the role card for the next lesson. The learner does not need to perform to the class.

stages.title: Key words
body: Hospitality: looking after guests and customers.
Business: provides goods or services.
Job role: work and responsibilities of a job.
Task: one piece of work.
Front of house: direct guest contact.
Back of house: behind-the-scenes support.
stages.notes: Untimed vocabulary reference. Read aloud and point to the matching picture cue on the vocabulary mat. Explain that a role may cross front/back boundaries; the terms are a useful starting distinction, not a rule about worth or status. Repeat the frame “A __ works at a __ and __.”

support_pages.title: Business cards
lines: Cut apart or point. Use one business card at a time.
Café: customers buy light meals and drinks.
Event catering: food and drink for an event.
Pub: food and drink for customers.

support_pages.title: Job role cards
lines: Match a role to a business. A role may fit more than one business.

headers: Typical classroom example of a task
rows: Takes an order and serves it.
Takes food to the correct table.
Sets out food for an event.
Welcomes customers and checks their needs.

support_pages.title: Choose and explain
lines: Supported: choose a business card, then choose two roles. Say a task for each.
MCQ access: Hotel — receptionist / bus driver / housekeeper. Which two fit the model?
Independent: use your own examples beyond the cards where you can.
Aspire: name a role people may overlook and explain what happens if it is missing.
Frames: A __ works at a __ and __. I chose __ because __.

evidence_pages.title: My contribution to the shared mind map
instructions: Add one business type and one role in your own words. Put your name or learner code on the sticky note.
Mark your own note in the photo and record its reference.
fields: My note can be found at: __________

evidence_pages.title: My Business and Jobs record
instructions: Name five business types. For each one, give two job roles and one task for each role.
Circle the job role that interests you most.

paragraphs: Check the learner’s signed and agreed hospitality Plan under the supplied workbook’s rule. Bring that learner’s own prior Plan for the arrival retrieval. Supported includes a picture/card matching route and numbered prompts. Independent supplies examples and tasks. Aspire explains the value of an overlooked role. The routes reach the same core outcome; support and exact choices are recorded.

planner_sections.heading: Minutes record
paragraphs: Planned hospitality time is 40 minutes. Actual date, actual active minutes, contribution, support and adult initials stay blank until taught. Follow the workbook’s signed-Plan rule. Never count attendance as a completed evidence item and never add Careers minutes to hospitality time. [VERIFY] Official programme minimum and credit wording before a certification claim.

staff_answers: Hotel model: receptionist checks bookings; housekeeper prepares rooms; chef prepares food; porter helps with luggage. Different roles may share tasks in a small business.

Possible five-business record: hotel (receptionist, housekeeper); café (café assistant, barista); restaurant (chef, server); event catering (catering assistant, kitchen porter); pub (front of house assistant, stock assistant). Accept other defensible combinations and accurate tasks.
Supported MCQ: receptionist and housekeeper match the hotel model; bus driver is the distractor. Explain rather than supplying an unrecorded assessed answer.
Evidence checks: own contribution marked; five businesses; ten roles; ten relevant tasks; one preferred role with the learner’s reason. A visible class map does not prove every learner contributed.
Do not infer eligibility, registered status, completed challenges or minutes from the model answers. The official student-book mapping is [VERIFY] until checked.
